majors.what: `commandBytes` calls `JSON.stringify(command.slide)` (and `JSON.stringify(command.theme)` at line 769) on a caller-supplied object, and `history.apply` calls it at history.ts:250 — *after* it has already committed the state change at history.ts:246-248 (`this.#doc = applied.doc; this.#rev += 1; this.#redo = []`). `structuredClone` accepts values `JSON.stringify` refuses: a BigInt and a cyclic reference are both cloneable and both make `JSON.stringify` throw. So the new `clone()` guard passes the payload through, the command applies, and then a bare `TypeError` escapes `apply()` with the document already changed and no history entry pushed. Verified end state after `apply([{t:'slide.insert', slide:{...entry, big:10n}, html:'x'}])`: `rev 1, undoDepth 0, redoDepth 0, canUndo false, slide present in manifest, slideOrder length 2` — the slide is in the document and cannot be undone. Stack trace: `JSON.stringify -> commandBytes (commands.ts:762) -> batchBytes (history.ts:120) -> DocumentHistory.apply (history.ts:250)`. Reproduced identically for a cyclic `SlideEntry` key ('Converting circular structure to JSON') and for `deck.setTheme` carrying a BigInt. The extra key reaches the document because `applySlideInsert` deliberately keeps the object it built rather than zod's stripped output (verified: an entry with `extra:'LEAKED'` is stored verbatim in `manifest.slides`), which is a documented choice — but it is what puts a non-JSON-able value in front of the byte accounting.
majors.why: This is the exact goal commit 764d2d3 set for itself and did not reach for this input class. The commit's stated aim is 'a total clone() helper mapping failure to typed error codes with batch-copy-before-apply so not-cloneable can't arrive mid-state-change'. For a BigInt or a cycle the failure did not become a value — it relocated, from the clone (which ran *before* any state change, exactly like the `DOMException` r2 rated a minor) to the byte accounting (which runs *after*). That relocation makes it strictly worse than what it replaced: the pre-fix `DOMException` threw with the document untouched, whereas this one leaves the document mutated, `rev` bumped, the redo stack cleared and no undo entry — 'a state change with no history entry' is the precise corruption commands.ts:28-33 and history.ts:13-16 say this layer exists to prevent, and it falsifies 'Never throws, never mutates' at commands.ts:529 and 'errors are values, never throws' at commands.ts:17. Not a blocker: no real producer can reach it today, since every command source is JSON (an IPC payload, an agent tool call, `.sloodge` bytes) and `JSON.parse` produces neither a BigInt nor a cycle — the same reachability class as the `not-cloneable` guard itself, which the commit nonetheless judged worth building.
majors.fix: Two independent halves, both cheap. (1) Ordering: move `const bytes = batchBytes(...)` above the three state-commit lines in `history.apply`, so any throw lands before the document changes — this alone restores the pre-fix guarantee. (2) Totality: a byte *estimate* has no business throwing at all — wrap the two `JSON.stringify` calls in `commandBytes` in a try/catch falling back to `overhead` (or reuse the `clone`-style total helper), which closes it completely and keeps the soft cap conservative. Worth one test each: a `slide.insert` whose entry carries `10n` should return a typed error (or a finite byte count), not throw.

majors.what: `apply([])` — an empty command batch — pushes a phantom undo entry and wipes the redo stack. `applyBatch` returns `{ok:true}` with an empty inverse for an empty batch, so `apply` falls through to `this.#rev += 1`, `this.#redo = []` and `#push({forward: [], inverse: [], ...})` with no length guard. Verified: after `apply(insert)` then `undo()` the history reports `canRedo true, redoLabel 'Delete slide'`; a following `apply([], {kind:'user', label:'No-op tool call'})` reports `canRedo false, undoDepth 1, undoLabel 'No-op tool call'`, and pressing Ctrl+Z on that entry returns `ok:true` with the document byte-identical — a visible no-op undo. The sibling path guards this correctly: `commitTransaction` at history.ts:337 wraps `#push` in `if (open.forward.length > 0)` and an empty transaction leaves `undoDepth 0` (verified).
majors.why: history.ts:330-332 states the principle in its own words — 'an empty undo step would consume a Ctrl+Z and do nothing visible, which reads as a broken undo' — and then `apply` violates it, undocumented, two methods above. The redo-stack loss is the sharper harm: a batch that did nothing silently destroys work the user could have redone, which no amount of reading `apply`'s docblock would predict. Not a blocker because no caller exists yet (`DocumentSession` is future work), but an empty batch is exactly what a well-behaved producer emits — an agent tool call that resolves to no changes, a design-mode drag that coalesces to nothing — and the bug it produces ('undo did nothing', 'my redo disappeared') is a miserable one to trace back to a zero-length array.
majors.fix: Return early when `commands.length === 0`, before the `rev` bump and the redo clear: `if (commands.length === 0) return { ok: true, doc: this.#doc, rev: this.#rev }`. That matches `commitTransaction`'s existing guard and keeps the two paths saying the same thing. One test: apply an edit, undo it, apply an empty batch, assert `canRedo` is still true and `undoDepth` is unchanged.

minors.what: Nit: the not-cloneable error path builds its message from `command.t` — a read of the caller's object performed *after* that object has already proven hostile. A `Proxy` whose `get` trap throws on `'t'` makes `apply` throw the trap's error instead of returning `{code:'not-cloneable'}` (verified: `THREW: Error: T-TRAP`). State is untouched (`rev 0`, `canUndo false`, document identical by reference), so this is a contract nit rather than a correctness one.
minors.why: Only worth a line because the whole point of the surrounding code is that this boundary fails as a value. A general throwing-getter payload and a general throwing-trap Proxy both work correctly (both return `not-cloneable` with state untouched) — it is specifically the discriminant read in the error message that is unguarded, and a Proxy is a long way from any real producer.
minors.fix: Drop `command.t` from the message, or read it once into a local before the clone loop.

r2_findings_reverified.minor_1_DOMException_escape: FIXED for the class it named, with one relocation raised as major 1 above. hypotheses_tested: `clone()` is not total — a getter that throws, a Proxy with a throwing get trap, a BigInt. SPLIT: REJECTED for the getter and the general Proxy (both return `not-cloneable`, state untouched, verified by reference identity). CONFIRMED for BigInt, but not where expected — `structuredClone` *accepts* BigInt, so the clone succeeds and the throw surfaces downstream in `commandBytes`, after the state change. Raised as major 1.

A non-cloneable payload can arrive mid-state-change. REJECTED for the case the commit designed against: a batch whose second command is non-cloneable never touches the document (`rev 0, undoDepth 0, redoDepth 0`, doc identical by reference), and the same inside an open transaction leaves the transaction open and unchanged. CONFIRMED for the BigInt/cycle case, which bypasses the clone boundary entirely — the substance of major 1.

The clone-before-validate order opens a TOCTOU window rather than closing one. REJECTED — instrumented a `title` getter returning 'First' then 'Second'; it is read exactly once and 'First' is what lands in the document, so validation and storage see the same bytes.

The undo stack's `forward` commands alias either the caller's object or the live document. REJECTED — after `apply`, the stacked `slide` is `!==` the caller's entry and `!==` the manifest entry, and mutating the stacked entry's title leaves the document reading 'Untitled slide'. Three distinct copies, as designed.

Empty batch handling is inconsistent between `apply` and `commitTransaction`. CONFIRMED — `apply([])` pushes a phantom entry and clears the redo stack (`canRedo` true -> false), while an empty transaction correctly pushes nothing. Raised as major 2.
Undo/redo of a non-commuting pair drifts. REJECTED — insert-then-move, undone twice, is `JSON.stringify`-identical to the pre-state, and redoing twice restores the moved slide to index 0.
The `cloneCommand` signature change stranded a caller. REJECTED — one caller (history.ts:236), typecheck green, no other module imports from `document/commands` outside tests.

notes.summary: The fix commit does what it says on all three r2 findings, and I verified each by mutation rather than by reading: the depth of `cloneCommand` is now the sole red under a depth-only mutant, the byte term is pinned by shape, and the drifted comment is accurate. The copy boundary is genuinely total for the payload class it was written against. What it does not cover is the payload class `structuredClone` *accepts* and `JSON.stringify` rejects — a BigInt or a cyclic reference sails through the clone, applies to the document, and then throws a bare `TypeError` out of `commandBytes` at history.ts:250, after `rev` has bumped and the redo stack has been cleared but before any undo entry is pushed. That leaves the document changed and un-undoable, which is worse than the `DOMException` the commit replaced, since that one threw before any state change. Neither that nor the empty-batch phantom entry is reachable from a real producer today; both are two lines to close, and the ordering half of the first fix (compute `bytes` before committing the state) is worth doing regardless.
